scope: DFS/CAC startup recognition shared by AP readiness, ordinary toggles, runtime repair, native configuration application and original AP recovery
confirmed_feedback: OpenWrt 23.05.4, HE160, hostapd DFS-CAC-START cac_time=60s; AP-ENABLED about 65 seconds later; prior 45-second deadline failed first.

proof.fallback: Only missing BSS object plus administrative UP and no carrier; bounded timestamped hostapd logs, exact interface or live sysfs phy match; no guessed radio numbering
proof.ready: CAC evidence never means ready. Existing live hostapd/kernel positive AP verification is still required.

bounds.native_apply: Original rpcd rollback is 90 seconds. Device-driven extensions cannot exceed a conservative 80-second deadline started before stage; final confirmation has ten seconds reserved. Longer CAC is reported unconfirmed and recovery attempted.
bounds.logs: No raw SSID, credentials or router logs added to routine readiness evidence. Evidence is sanitized and transitions remain bounded.

compatibility.limitations: Source contracts and synthetic Lua devices only. Vendor-modified logread or evicted/missing CAC records may prevent detection; unsupported output never triggers a guessed delay.

builtin_package.verified: Formal seed_assets and make_zip executed in an isolated resource regression; archive member and SHA256 match, corrupt input rejected by verify_files.

release: Source changes only; no new full application package produced in this turn.

corrected: Backend runtime repair now rejects a snapshot already reporting active CAC before any wireless reload.
Native CAC without an event identifier recognizes an explicitly restarted countdown or a new active cycle; unchanged or missing remaining-time fields never renew the same cycle indefinitely.
review.regressions: 165 targeted tests passed, including native Lua readiness, virtual-time restarts, cancellation, native rollback limits, bridge/save/UI behavior, builtin resource collection and partial dependency installation.
review.scope_limit: No live router validation and no new full application release built.

second_review.root_case: Multiple BSS records on one live sysfs phy: an older own CAC start could override a newer sibling CAC cycle or revive after its completion.
second_review.resolution: Keep the most recent local BSS lifecycle and radio CAC lifecycle separately. Use observed log order, including equal millisecond stamps, and require positive duration before calling an event active. A sibling BSS stop does not cancel an ongoing radio CAC.
second_review.verification: 170 targeted tests passed on Windows; final code unchanged during run. Includes same-phy new cycles, completion followed by AP-ENABLED, local stop isolation, equal timestamps and integer-second/fractional-log precision.
second_review.platform_scope: Shared Python/Lua strategy, no new desktop OS branches. Debian 12 desktop startup, dependencies and shutdown remain unverified this turn.
pending_acceptance: On a real affected router, enable its 60-second DFS AP and confirm ready ends immediately after AP start.
Verify two same-radio APs and a new CAC cycle, cancellation and failed configuration recovery.
On Debian 12 x86-64 with application dependencies, verify imports/startup, signal task, dependency installation and exit cleanup.
second_review.source_scope: Existing exact-release get_status/logread source contracts preserved. Exact OpenWrt 23.05.4 logd tail ordering re-read. No claim that vendor firmware or all physical chipsets passed live testing.
